about: pane-pulse decision table. The single source of truth shared by three readers: hook/hook.js (CommonJS, zero deps, reads this file from beside itself), src/decision.ts and tests/contract.test.mjs. One row per (event, matcher, agent_id, bg) region. The regions are disjoint and, once the normalisation block below has been applied, total: exactly one row matches any input, so nothing falls through and no row is shadowed. Apply the normalisation block first or the rows are NOT total -- that block is part of the contract, not a detail of any one reader. There is deliberately no focus dimension: the hook never decides whether the member was looking at a pane, it always sets the mark, and the VS Code extension owns every clear. Only an unread mark is ever cleared by looking at a pane; a waiting mark changes only when the state does, which is why a wrong focus guess can drop an unread mark and can never drop a waiting one. agent_id is present only inside a subagent call, so absent means the main thread and is the normal case. bg is background_tasks.length, a field the docs put on Stop and SubagentStop only. Event names and notification_type values verified against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks on 2026-09-20; the quotes were read from the documentation itself, not from memory. A row is registered when its (event, matcher-when-matcher_mode-is-in) key is listed in registrations below; registered rows are the only ones ever written into Claude Code's settings, each written in the shape its registration declares -- 'node' for the exec form that runs hook.js, 'shell' for the one-liner PostToolUse uses because it fires once per tool call -- and every other row still exists because the three readers share this contract. SessionStart is registered on its source -- startup, resume or clear, three of the five values the docs name -- so a pane is listed from the moment claude starts, and it prints nothing: those rows are idle with no sequence because a hook's plain stdout on SessionStart is added to Claude's context (a /clear's mark is already wiped by the SessionEnd row's own clear), while compact and fork stay unregistered no-ops so a mid-turn compaction never touches a spinner.

normalisation.about: Rules every reader applies to one event's payload BEFORE comparing it with a row. They live here, as data, because the three readers share no code: hook/hook.js is plain CommonJS and never imports src/decision.ts. The rows are NOT total on their own -- a Stop whose payload carries no background_tasks matches no bg row until absent_reads_as is applied, and a reader that skips this block emits no sequence and leaves that pane's spinner lit forever. Apply all three rules and the rows are total and unique: every input matches exactly one row, and none matches two. There is no focus rule here and there never will be: the hook reads no focus of any kind, so a pane's own payload is the whole input.

bg.rule: Read the payload's background_tasks as its array length. The docs put the field on Stop and SubagentStop only, and even there only when the task registry is reachable, so an absent field is a real state and never an error: a missing key or a null reads as absent_reads_as, and a present-but-unreadable value (not an array, not a finite number) reads as non_numeric_reads_as. Compare the resulting count with the row's bg as the compare table above says.

compare.absent: matches when the reading is absent
compare.present: matches when the reading is present

agent_id.rule: agent_id is present only when the hook fires inside a subagent call, so its absence means the main thread and is the normal case, never an error. A missing key, a null, a non-string and an empty string all read as absent; any other string reads as present.

compare.in: matches when the subject is a string equal to one whole alternative
compare.not-in: matches every other subject, including no subject at all

subject.rule: The subject is the payload field that subject_fields names for this event (source for SessionStart, tool_name for PreToolUse, notification_type for Notification); every other event has no subject at all. A missing key, a null or a non-string reads as no subject. A matcher is a '|'-separated list of exact, whole-string alternatives -- the doc's own exact-match matcher path -- never a regular expression, never a prefix.
